 THE TIMES OF INDIA | Nov 07, 2026, 12:52:44 IST SUMMARY India vs New Zealand Live Score, 2nd ODI: Wellington will host the next chapter of India's New Zealand tour as the teams prepare for the second ODI at Hnry Stadium on November 7. The visitors have already drawn first blood in the series, defeating the Black Caps by five wickets in a rain-shortened opening encounter. 
 India's success in Auckland was built on a disciplined bowling effort. Arshdeep Singh troubled the New Zealand batters throughout the innings, finishing with four wickets, while Gurnoor Brar and Anshul Kamboj also made significant contributions. Their efforts restricted the home team to 185. 
 The responsibility then fell on India's experienced batting line-up. Virat Kohli took charge with a fluent 74 off 51 deliveries, ensuring the visitors completed the revised 143-run target with five wickets remaining. Gill also chipped in with 37 runs. 
 New Zealand will need a much-improved performance, particularly from their top order. The absence of Devon Conway, who has been sidelined by concussion, adds to their concerns. Nick Kelly has joined the squad as his replacement. 
 Gill's impressive ODI numbers, Kohli's aggressive strokeplay and Rahul's consistency provide India with plenty of batting confidence. The hosts will look towards Daryl Mitchell and Mitchell Santner for a stronger response. 
 The contest also offers another opportunity for Gujarat Titans players Gill and Brar to make an impact. India will aim to move further ahead, while New Zealand will be fighting to prevent the visitors from establishing a commanding series advantage. The match starts at 7:30 AM IST. Commentary

 12:16 (IST) Nov 07 We are all set for India's reply. The two umpires and players make their way out to the middle. We have news coming in from the New Zealand camp that Matthew Fisher has been confirmed as a concussion substitute for Blair Tickner, who took a blow to the head while batting. Rohit Sharma and Shubman Gill walk out to open the innings for India. Kyle Jamieson has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. There is a slight delay before play can get underway as a patch of grass has come away around the slip region. A member of the ground staff brings out a bucket of soil and a hammer to fill the affected area and pat it down. A patch of fresh turf is brought in, and the ground staff use a grass saw to trim it to size. The repair work is done, and away we go...
 12:16 (IST) Nov 07 ... THE RUN CHASE ...
 11:59 (IST) Nov 07 Easy chase? Well, 135 is by no means a threatening target, especially with an in-form Indian top order with Kohli in prime form. New Zealand will have to bowl out of their skins to make a genuine match out of this. They must strike with the new ball, just like India did. But it is advantage India, with the tourists looking to get the job done without too much fuss. Rohit, meanwhile, will be keen to make amends for his first-ODI duck and get some runs under his belt. Back in a bit with the run chase. Stick around.
 11:58 (IST) Nov 07 Brar leads the pack - Just as the stand between Daryl Mitchell and Tom Latham was beginning to take shape, Gurnoor Brar landed a double blow, removing Latham and Phillips in the same over. New Zealand suddenly slumped to 53 for 5, with their innings going nowhere. Mitchell, though, kept fighting from one end. He stayed vigilant, brought up a well-earned half-century, and forged another 59-run recovery stand with Santner before Axar broke it by dismissing Mitchell. Gurnoor then struck again immediately after, sending Santner packing to leave New Zealand reeling at 119 for 7. And from there, the Kiwis just came crashing down in a hurry. Gurnoor finished with a four-for, whereas the likes of Kamboj, Auqib Nabi and Axar picked two apiece, with only Arshdeep staying wicketless and not even needed for his final spell.
 11:54 (IST) Nov 07 Runs at a premium - Make hay while the sun shines, they say, and India did exactly that. Winning a vital toss after a rain delay, they bowled under heavy skies on a surface carrying moisture, with conditions seemingly designed for seam bowling. Arshdeep, Kamboj and Nabi suffocated the batters with disciplined lines and relentless 6-8-metre lengths. Kamboj and Nabi were the first ones to land those initial blows, tearing through the top order and leaving the hosts dented at 23/3. Runs were hard to come by as Mitchell, dropped on 21 by Gill, and Latham came together to rebuild the innings.
 11:53 (IST) Nov 07 In conversation with Daryl Mitchell - Daryl says it was pretty challenging out there, with the pitch offering unpredictable bounce. Mentions that it felt like batting on a trampoline, and they were never quite sure how high the ball would bounce. Shares that they tried to scrape their way through but found it difficult to rotate the strike. Adds that due to the drop in wickets and no wickets on the square, dropping and running is tough. He says they wanted to keep extending the partnerships but lost wickets whenever they looked to build something. Mitchell feels there is still plenty in the pitch for the seamers and believes that if they can pick up a couple of early wickets, anything can happen.
 302 More Updates Load More India vs New Zealand Live Score, 2nd ODI: The battle for ODI supremacy between India and New Zealand moves to Wellington, where the two sides will meet in the second match of their five-game series on Saturday, November 7. India have the advantage after beginning the tour with a convincing five-wicket win in Auckland, but the hosts will be determined to put that disappointment behind them.
Shubman Gill's side had plenty of positives to take from the opening encounter, particularly the performance of its pace attack. Arshdeep Singh led the wicket-taking charts with four dismissals, while Gurnoor Brar and Anshul Kamboj contributed three and two wickets respectively. New Zealand were dismissed for 185, allowing India to take control of the contest.
The chase was largely shaped by Virat Kohli, whose 74-run innings from just 51 balls helped India reach the revised DLS target of 143 in 22.4 overs. Gill played a supporting role with 37, although the captain will be hoping to spend more time at the crease in the next game.
The home side, meanwhile, must address its batting shortcomings. Its task has become more challenging with Devon Conway unavailable for the rest of the series following a concussion in training. Nick Kelly has been added to the squad as cover.
Individual performances could play a major role in deciding the Wellington encounter. Gill has accumulated 3,701 ODI runs since 2022 at an average of 66.1, while KL Rahul has maintained an average of 63.7 when batting between positions four and six since 2023. Kohli's ability to attack pull and hook deliveries was another notable feature of the previous game.
Daryl Mitchell, who scored 28 in Auckland, will be among the players New Zealand expect to deliver a bigger contribution.
With India chasing another victory and New Zealand desperate for a response, the Wellington fixture promises to be an important moment in the series. The match begins at 7:30 AM IST.
